newsitem.title: INDONESIA: ASEAN businessmen oppose trade, labour linkage.
newsitem.headline: ASEAN businessmen oppose trade, labour linkage.

text.p: Business leaders from the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) agreed on Tuesday to back their governments in preventing labour standards from being included in trade issues.

The annual meeting of the ASEAN Chambers of Commerce and Industry (ASEAN-CCI) decided it would participate more actively at international gatherings, including the World Trade Organisation (WTO) and the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation forum, to prevent linking the two issues, said Jose Concepcion Jr, the group's executive committee chairman.
Developing nations, including ASEAN, opposed the linkage between trade and labour at the inaugural ministerial meeting of the WTO in Singapore in December.

"It will be unrealistic to assume that these issues have been put to rest," Concepcion told reporters after the day-long ASEAN-CCI meeting. "Developing countries must therefore prepare fully for these multilateral negotiations."
ASEAN groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.

Concepcion said the business leaders reviewed trends and opportunities that would emerge in the region by 2020, when he said ASEAN would have one billion consumers and gross domestic product of $2.0 trillion.
He said the businessmen decided to make efforts to eradicate poverty in the region by 2020.
"If we can increase the per capita income of over 50 percent of our people in the region, who are below the poverty line, then we will have increased (our) market," he said.
The ASEAN-CCI begins a two-day meeting with business leaders from trading partner nations on Wednesday, expected to be attended by more than 600 delegates.
More than 200 of them are from the United States, organisers have said.
ASEAN-CCI president Aburizal Bakrie told reporters the ASEAN Business Summit would be held every two years, with the next meeting scheduled for 1999 in Kuala Lumpur.
